title: Tanzanian Coconut Water
community: Zanzibar and the coast — the original sports drink of the Indian Ocean
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Maji ya Nazi — a young green coconut hacked open with a machete and drunk directly through a straw. The most natural, most hydrating, and most Zanzibari drink — the coconut water of a freshly opened young coconut is nature's finest electrolyte drink.
longDesc: Young coconut water in Zanzibar is the drink of the island's hottest hours — vendors with piles of green coconuts and machetes are a fixture at every Zanzibar beach and market. One decisive machete chop, a straw inserted, and the cool, sweet, slightly nutty water of the young coconut is the most refreshing thing available on the island.
steps: Hold the coconut firmly on a stable surface.
With a heavy machete, make 3—4 decisive chopping cuts to the top to create an opening.
Or: cut away the top in a conical shape with successive clean cuts.
When finished, crack the coconut open and eat the soft young coconut flesh with a spoon.
chefTips: Buy young (green) coconuts only — the older brown coconuts have reduced water and different flavour.
The coconut should feel heavy with water when shaken.
Eat the soft jelly-like flesh inside after drinking — it is equally nourishing.
commonMistakes: Buying mature coconuts — not the same drink.
cookingScience: Young coconut water is isotonic — it contains the same concentration of electrolytes (potassium, sodium, magnesium) as human blood plasma, making it uniquely effective for rapid rehydration. It was used as intravenous fluid in emergency situations during World War II due to its sterility and electrolyte profile.
sustainabilityTips: The coconut palm provides water, food (flesh), oil (mature coconut), fibre (coir), and shelter (leaves) from one tree. The most sustainable possible drink source.
storage: Drink immediately after opening. Refrigerate unused portion 24 hours.
healthBenefits: Low in sugar compared to other fruit juices.
One of nature's finest hydration drinks.
culturalNote: Fresh coconut water from a just-hacked green coconut at a Zanzibar beach — drunk in the shade of a palm tree, with the Indian Ocean in front of you — is one of the island's most perfect simple pleasures. The machete, the coconut, the straw — it has been this way on the coast for as long as coconut palms have grown here.
